lead: Working stress method (WSM) checks a reinforced concrete section at service loads. The section is assumed elastic: plane sections remain plane, concrete is linear in compression, concrete carries no tension, and steel and concrete act together. Stresses computed from these assumptions must stay below permissible values. WSM is used for simple beams, older structures, and preliminary checks. It is also called the elastic method or service load method.
prereq: You need Chapter 1.1 for stress–strain behaviour and modular ratio.

sections.h3: Service loads, elastic stresses and permissible limits

blocks.text: WSM starts with service loads: the loads expected during normal use, without load factors. Elastic analysis gives concrete compressive stress σ<sub>cbc</sub> and steel tensile stress σ<sub>st</sub>. A permissible stress is the code limit for that stress at service. For M20 concrete in bending, σ<sub>cbc</sub> = 7 N/mm². For Fe415 steel in tension, σ<sub>st</sub> = 230 N/mm².

items: Plane sections remain plane, so strain varies linearly with distance from the neutral axis.
Concrete in compression is linear elastic: stress is proportional to strain.
Concrete tension is ignored; steel carries all tension after cracking.
Steel and concrete at the same level have the same strain. The modular ratio m converts steel area into equivalent concrete area.

blocks.where: m is the modular ratio; E<sub>s</sub> is Young's modulus of steel; E<sub>c</sub> is an effective modulus of concrete; σ<sub>cbc</sub> is the permissible concrete compressive stress in N/mm².

blocks.text: For M20 with σ<sub>cbc</sub> = 7 N/mm², m = 280/(3×7) = 13.33. This value accounts for creep under long-term compression.

sections.h3: Balanced section: k, j and Q

blocks.text: In a balanced section, concrete and steel reach their permissible stresses at the same moment. Let x be the neutral axis depth and d the effective depth. The neutral axis depth factor is k = x/d. Strain compatibility and the modular ratio give the balanced value of k.

blocks.where: k is the neutral axis depth factor; m is the modular ratio; σ<sub>cbc</sub> is the permissible concrete compressive stress; σ<sub>st</sub> is the permissible steel tensile stress.
j is the lever arm factor; the lever arm is z = jd.

blocks.text: M<sub>R</sub> = 0.5σ<sub>cbc</sub> b x z = Q b d²
blocks.where: M<sub>R</sub> is the moment of resistance in Nmm; b is the beam width in mm; d is the effective depth in mm; Q is the moment factor in N/mm², with Q = 0.5σ<sub>cbc</sub> k j.

blocks.text: For M20 concrete and Fe415 steel, m = 13.33, k = 0.2887, j = 0.9038 and Q = 0.913 N/mm². Rounded, k = 0.289 and j = 0.904. A section with less steel than the balanced value is governed by steel; a section with more steel is governed by concrete.

sections.h3: Design of a singly reinforced rectangular beam

blocks.text: WSM design fixes a rectangular section and tension steel so that elastic stresses stay within permissible values.

items: Find the service bending moment M from the applied loads.
Choose width b and effective depth d. Effective depth is overall depth minus cover minus half the bar diameter.
Compute m, k, j and Q for the chosen concrete and steel.
Find the balanced moment capacity M<sub>R</sub> = Q b d². If M is greater, increase the depth.
Find required steel area A<sub>st</sub> = M / (σ<sub>st</sub> j d).
Choose bars giving at least this area, then check cover and spacing.
Check shear and bond separately; flexure design alone is not enough.

blocks.text: The method is simple and conservative because permissible stresses are well below strength. It does not predict collapse or ductility. Full beam design, flanged sections and doubly reinforced sections belong to Unit 2; shear belongs to Unit 3.

examples.question: A singly reinforced rectangular beam has b = 230 mm and d = 450 mm. Use M20 concrete with σcbc = 7 N/mm² and Fe415 steel with σst = 230 N/mm². Find the balanced moment of resistance and the balanced steel area.
steps: Neutral axis depth factor: k = mσcbc / (mσcbc + σst) = (13.33 × 7) / (13.33 × 7 + 230) = 93.33 / 323.33 = 0.2887, about 0.289.
Lever arm factor: j = 1 − k/3 = 1 − 0.2887/3 = 0.9038, about 0.904.
Moment factor: Q = 0.5σcbc k j = 0.5 × 7 × 0.2887 × 0.9038 = 0.913 N/mm².
Balanced moment: MR = Q b d² = 0.913 × 230 × 450² = 42.5 × 10⁶ Nmm = 42.5 kNm.
Balanced steel area: Ast = MR / (σst j d) = 42.5 × 10⁶ / (230 × 0.9038 × 450) = 454 mm².
examples.answer: The balanced moment of resistance is 42.5 kNm and the balanced steel area is 454 mm².
examples.check:
b = 230.0
d = 450.0
scbc = 7.0
sst = 230.0
m = 280 / (3 * scbc)
k = (m * scbc) / (m * scbc + sst)
j = 1 - k / 3
Q = 0.5 * scbc * k * j
m_ans = round(m, 2)
k_ans = round(k, 3)
j_ans = round(j, 3)
Q_ans = round(Q, 3)
MR_kNm = Q_ans * b * d * d / 1e6
Ast = MR_kNm * 1e6 / (sst * j_ans * d)
print(f'{m_ans:.2f}')
print(f'{k_ans:.3f}')
print(f'{j_ans:.3f}')
print(f'{Q_ans:.3f}')
print(f'{MR_kNm:.1f}')
print(f'{round(Ast):.0f}')

traps: Do not use fy = 415 N/mm² as σst. WSM uses the permissible stress, here 230 N/mm² for Fe415.
Concrete carries no tension in WSM. All tensile force is taken by steel.
The formula m = 280/(3σcbc) uses σcbc, not σst. Both stresses must be in N/mm².
Balanced section means concrete and steel reach permissible stress together. A real section may be under-reinforced or over-reinforced.
WSM uses service loads with no load factors or partial safety factors. Limit state design uses factored loads.

quiz.q: Define modular ratio m in WSM.
quiz.a: m = Es/Ec, the ratio of steel modulus to concrete modulus. For WSM, m = 280/(3σcbc).

quiz.q: Why is concrete tension ignored in WSM?
quiz.a: Concrete has low tensile strength and cracks at small tensile strain. Steel is assumed to carry all tension after cracking.

quiz.q: For M20 concrete with σcbc = 7 N/mm² and Fe415 steel with σst = 230 N/mm², find k.
A beam has more steel than the balanced amount. Which material reaches its permissible stress first?
quiz.a: Concrete reaches its permissible compressive stress first. The section is over-reinforced in WSM and concrete governs.

quiz.q: A rectangular beam has b = 250 mm and d = 500 mm. Use Q = 0.913 N/mm². Find the balanced moment of resistance.
Why is WSM called the elastic method?
quiz.a: It assumes plane sections remain plane and concrete is linear elastic in compression, so stresses follow elastic theory.

quiz.q: Why does WSM not directly prove safety against collapse?
quiz.a: WSM checks service stresses against permissible values. It does not model ultimate load, plastic behaviour, or ductility, so collapse safety is not directly calculated.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern concrete design in India mainly uses limit state method. WSM still appears in checks of old structures, masonry, and simple water-retaining sections. Software uses transformed sections and modular ratio for service stress checks. Search next for working stress method IS 456, balanced section, transformed section, and modular ratio.
